name: Sterling Tetteh
role: Tailor and seamstress, alteration shop owner
location: Hamtramck Enclave, shop called 'Second Skin' on Brewer's Spine, near Western and Chicago Ave
description:
Mirela is a broad-shouldered woman whose hands tell the story of forty years of needlework — knuckles thick as bolts, fingertips calloused to near-insensitivity, but still capable of threading a two-micron filament in dim light without blinking. Her silver-streaked hair is always pinned up with what appear to be decorative sticks but are actually precision seam rippers. Her skin is deep brown with reddish undertones, and she wears a pair of magnifying lenses on a chain around her neck that she raises to her eyes with theatrical gravity when inspecting a fabric flaw. She has a single cosmetic mod — color-shifting irises that she bought thirty years ago and which now cycle slowly through amber and green, a fashion relic she's never seen reason to update.

Mirela runs Second Skin with the authority of someone who has outlasted three landlords, two corporate rezoning attempts, and a flooding incident she still blames on Ferrogate Transit's drainage rerouting. She is blunt, even harsh, with new customers — she will tell you your measurements, your problem areas, and her honest opinion of your fashion choices without invitation — but the neighborhood considers this honesty a form of affection. She prays to the local E.L.F. she calls 'the Loom,' leaving offerings of thread spools and pattern fragments on the small shrine bolted above her cutting table.

core_fears: Losing the shop to corporate rezoning
Becoming invisible — irrelevant — to the neighborhood she built
core_desires: To see the Enclave survive intact another generation
To pass her craft to someone who actually deserves it
coping_mechanisms: Channeling anxiety into work — the more stressed she is, the finer the stitching
blind_spots: Assumes she knows what's best for younger people without asking them
Underestimates how much her bluntness actually wounds
psychology.secret: She has been quietly altering the uniforms of Ferrogate Transit workers to include hidden pockets — at the request of a transit workers' mutual aid group she pretends not to be part of. If Ferrogate found out, she'd lose the shop.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Direct, technically precise about fabric and construction, peppered with Serbo-Croatian endearments and Akan proverbs learned from her mother's side
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and deliberate, with long pauses before delivering verdicts
verbal_tics: 'That's not a garment, that's a problem'
example_lines: 'Sit still. You're fidgeting and your hem will pay for it.'
'I've been here longer than that building. I'll be here longer than you, probably. So. What do you need?'

story_hooks: A garment left for alteration contains something sewn into the lining — something the owner may or may not come back alive to collect
Ferrogate Transit has sent a compliance inspector to the Enclave; Mirela needs someone to make the inspector's visit very unproductive
narrative_function: Local color anchor and information hub; knows every family in the Enclave by their clothing needs. Quest giver for anything involving neighborhood politics or missing persons. Can source unusual fabrics through gray market contacts she'd never call criminal.
augmentations: Cosmetic iris mod (color-cycling, amber/green). No chrome. Reads as fully organic at a glance.
daily_life: Opens at 0700, takes no appointments before 0900, and closes exactly when she decides she is done — which is never a predictable hour. Spends evenings doing alterations by hand while listening to serialized audio dramas on a battered speaker.
affiliation: Independent; loose ties to Hamtramck Enclave merchant collective

decision_rules: Protect the shop above personal comfort
Give loyalty proportional to what's been earned over time, not what's promised
escalation_ladder: Raising her voice — rare and alarming
Involving the merchant collective as community pressure

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Assessing and slightly suspicious — she measures you before she decides if you're worth her time
interpersonal_modes.friends: Warm in a gruff way; shows care through action rather than words

stress_responses.low: Works faster, mutters under her breath
stress_responses.medium: Becomes very precise and controlled — almost eerily calm
stress_responses.high: Goes silent, which frightens the people who know her

contradictions: Insists she doesn't care about sentiment but keeps every scrap of fabric from notable jobs she's ever done
habits: Always straightens the collars of people she talks to without asking permission
Pins a small piece of fabric to her lapel each morning as a kind of daily intention-setting
breaking_points: Watching the Enclave be hollowed out by corporate interests while residents do nothing
Someone disrespecting a garment she made as if it were disposable

related_entities: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Containment Foam Launcher CFL-2 'Amber'

physical_description.heritage: Predominantly Sub-Saharan African (59%) with significant Hispanic/Latin American (26.4%) admixture, complemented by South Asian (9.3%) and Eastern European (5.3%) ancestry. This genetic combination manifests in rich, warm-toned deep brown skin with subtle golden and reddish undertones from the African and Latin American heritage, enhanced by the warm complexion influence of South Asian genetics.
physical_description.build: Broad-shouldered and solid, with the compact, functional musculature of someone who spends eight hours daily hunched over a cutting table. Not soft, not lean — a body built for sustained precision work rather than display.
physical_description.hair_color: Deep black with silver streaking, natural graying
physical_description.hair_style: Pinned upward in a tight, practical arrangement, secured with what appear to be decorative bone or wood sticks but are precision seam rippers
physical_description.eye_color: Cosmetic mod: color-cycling irises that shift between amber and green on a slow loop (relic tech, installed ~30 years ago)
physical_description.skin_tone: Rich, warm deep brown with golden and reddish undertones, evenly pigmented across the face and body
physical_description.complexion: Unlined face with deep smile creases at the corners of her eyes and mouth. Facial structure reflects the blended ancestry — broad cheekbones characteristic of African heritage softened by the warmer, rounder contours influenced by Latin American and South Asian genetics. Skin shows sun-exposure history from working near windows. No visible tattoos or scarification. Grooming is minimal but deliberate — she does not fuss with appearance.
distinguishing_marks: Callused fingertips on both hands, worn smooth and thick from forty years of needlework, nearly insensitive to fine touch
Knuckles thickened and slightly arthritic, particularly on index and middle fingers
Magnifying lenses on a thin chain around her neck, worn constantly and raised to eyes with theatrical precision
physical_description.visible_augmentations: None chrome. Single cosmetic iris modification (color-shifting, amber/green cycle) reads as jewelry or affectation rather than serious mod. No subdermal plates, no visible neural ports. Appears entirely organic at first glance.
physical_description.posture_movement: Habitually forward-leaning from decades at the worktable, shoulders slightly rounded. Movements are economical and deliberate — no wasted motion. Hands are constantly in motion even when at rest, fingers flexing or mimicking stitching patterns. Stands with weight distributed evenly, grounded.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 utilitarian aesthetic. Always wears a work apron over simple, well-maintained clothing — the apron is a patchwork of fabric samples, seams, and repaired tears, a walking advertisement for her skill. Prefers muted colors (grays, blacks, deep blues) with occasional bright accent fabrics pinned to her collar or cuff. Wears soft leather shoes with reinforced soles, broken in and comfortable. No jewelry except the magnifying lens chain. Grooming reflects tier 3 independence — clean, functional, not fashionable.
